clue.text: Coming round naked, stripped and wrapped in canopy

indicators.note: the trimmed word sits inside the canopy word, which is wrapped round it

parts.note: an awning is a canopy over a door or window

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, the word naked loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is coming to, unclothed and bundled up in a tent's canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming round' reads as part of the scene but is the definition; 'stripped' removes the first and last letters of the bare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Regaining consciousness is a synonym for coming round, a sense of waking.

clue.text: Scientist moving north, engaged by defence expert

indicators.note: engaged by means held within, so the scrambled word goes inside the defence expert

parts.note: an apologist is someone who argues in defence of a cause

indicators.note: moving signals that the letters of north are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A researcher heading north is hired by someone skilled in defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving north' looks like travel but signals the scrambled compass word, which 'engaged by' tucks in just after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthropologist is a scientist who studies human societies and cultures.

clue.text: A bit of sun seen around book's romantic land

indicators.note: around means the ray goes round the letter for book

parts.note: a ray is a beam, a small bit of sunlight

explanation.surface: A glimpse of sunshine surrounds a novel set in some idealised country.
explanation.walkthrough: Araby is a poetic name for Arabia, and the title of a Joyce story about romantic longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Araby is the old poetic name for Arabia, a land of exotic romance in literature.

clue.text: US disease study to proceed, and proceed slowly, failing to end up before year

indicators.note: before places the reversed pieces ahead of the year letter
in a down entry, up means the pieces are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to go is to proceed

indicators.note: failing to end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to loiter is to dawdle, proceeding slowly

explanation.surface: An American medical research programme is told to press on slowly, unfinished before the year is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to end' makes LOITE; 'up' turns GO plus LOITE into ETIOLOG. Etiology is the American spelling of aetiology.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiology is the American spelling of the branch of medicine studying the causes of disease.

clue.text: Popular description encapsulating Independent for the moment

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the description word holds the letter for Independent

parts.note: a term is a word used to describe something

explanation.surface: A catchy label containing the newspaper's name is good enough for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means provisional or temporary, holding only for the time being.

clue.text: Is sad, cut up about one after end of suffering

indicators.note: after puts the remaining wordplay behind that last letter
end of picks the last letter of the word suffering
about means going around, so the reversed cut word surrounds one
in a down entry, up means the word is written backwards

parts.note: to sever is to cut
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is upset, distressed over a person once the pain is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEVER into REVES, which goes 'about' I to make RIEVES, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to feel sorrow, so grieves matches is sad as a present-tense verb.

clue.text: Opening line's swamped by drunk

indicators.note: swamped by means engulfed, so the line letter goes inside the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A first remark gets drowned out by a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a narrow opening, like one for coins.

clue.text: Vision coming through slowly, having no power

indicators.note: having no means the power letter is taken away

parts.note: to seep is to come through slowly, as liquid does
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Sight gradually returns, though without much strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing is the faculty of sight, the same as vision.

clue.text: Working with those people, mostly about going places

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
them refers to those people

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: over means about, as in arguing over something

explanation.surface: Employed alongside a group of people, largely travelling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Going places means travelling, and the phrase describes someone in motion.

clue.text: Everyone oddly insouciant following hot fantasies

indicators.note: following places the word for everyone after the hot letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
all means everyone

indicators.note: oddly signals that the letters of insouciant are arranged in an odd, new way

explanation.surface: Everybody strangely carefree after a heatwave has wild daydreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns INSOUCIANT into UCINATIONS. 'oddly' does not mean alternate letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallucinations are perceptions of things not there, imagined visions or fantasies.

clue.text: Old Russian man blocking suggestion mostly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole build reads backwards
blocking means the man sits in the middle of the shortened word
mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: a taste is a slight suggestion, as in a taste of garlic
sir is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man of old Russia stands in the way of an idea that is mostly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' makes TAST; SIR goes in it to give TSIRAST, which 'rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist was a supporter of the tsar's rule, so a Russian of former times.

clue.text: Most of Aintree jumping blocked by one's unwillingness to move

indicators.note: blocked by means a letter gets in the way within the jumbled letters
jumping signals that the letters leap about into a new order
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Most racing at the Grand National course is held up by one horse that refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National steeplechase. 'Most of' leaves AINTRE; 'jumping' rearranges it to INERTA, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a reluctance to act or change, a tendency to stay still.

clue.text: King — true — not initially kinglike

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: loyal means true or faithful

explanation.surface: A monarch who is faithful but not at first regal.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means of or befitting a monarch, hence kinglike.

clue.text: Crime writer penning one volume featuring Tolkien location

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the writer's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Ruth Rendell was an English crime novelist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A detective novelist writes a single book that includes Middle-earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivendell is the elven refuge in Tolkien's The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Someone with the wrong number of ribs?

definitions.text: Someone with the wrong number of ribs?

parts.words: Someone with the wrong number of ribs?
parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a rib is jokingly a wife; having too many of them is a marital offence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribs' looks anatomical; in the Genesis story Eve was formed from Adam's rib, giving 'rib' as jocular slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A person married to several spouses at once has more wives than the law allows.

clue.text: Oil in USA misused by American here?

definitions.text: Oil in USA misused by American here?

indicators.note: misused signals the letters of the phrase are put to wrong use, rearranged

explanation.surface: An American state where oil gets wasted by its own people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges OIL IN USA into LOUISIAN; the whole clue also describes the place, an oil-producing state.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a Gulf Coast US state known for its oil industry.

clue.text: Bad source of liquor should have stone removed

indicators.note: removed means the stone abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: a still is the apparatus that distils spirits
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A poor distillery ought to have its gravel taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the stone, a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill means bad or harmful, as in ill effects.

clue.text: Band's extreme position in topic?

definitions.meaning: a neck ring of twisted metal worn by ancient Celts
the letter at either extreme of the word topic is ..., read as a phrase

explanation.surface: A musical group's furthest position on a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: the end letters of 'topic' are T or C.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a twisted metal collar, a band worn around the neck in Celtic times.

clue.text: Male that is gathering farm produce gets a headache

indicators.note: gathering means collecting inside, so the two letters surround the produce

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
grain is a crop produced on farms

explanation.surface: A man gathering in the harvest ends up with a pounding head.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe, recurring kind of headache.

clue.text: Looked threatening, though not about to be thundery?

indicators.note: not means the following word's letters are removed

parts.note: to lour is to look dark and threatening, as the sky does
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The sky looked menacing, but it wasn't going to thunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' and 'to be' are linking words; the question mark flags that thundery means noisy here.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundery is used loosely for noisy and booming, which is what loud means.

clue.text: Some potential space to inscribe one name of French writer

parts.note: a volt is a unit of electric potential

indicators.note: to inscribe here means to write inside, so one goes into the space word

parts.note: an area is a space
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bit of electrical energy, room to write a single French author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltairean is the adjective for things relating to Voltaire, the French satirist.

clue.text: Lump of stone not wanted in farm produce?

parts.note: out means rejected or no longer wanted
a crop is produce grown on a farm

explanation.surface: A rock lies unwelcome amid a field's harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of rock that sticks out above the ground.

clue.text: Current line in what could be maple syrup

indicators.note: in places the current and line letters inside the plant word

parts.note: a maple is an example of a tree
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A flow of maple syrup down a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maple syrup' looks like one phrase; 'what could be maple' is TREE and 'syrup' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a dark sticky syrup made from refining sugar.

clue.text: Faults besetting old expresses

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the faults word goes round the letter

parts.note: vices are moral faults

explanation.surface: Weaknesses plaguing an elderly person are spoken of.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it, so voices works as a verb.

clue.text: It fuels gossip and courage

parts.note: gas is idle chatter or gossip
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Something that drives rumour-mongering and bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas bottle is a cylinder holding fuel for a stove or heater.

clue.text: Just a shock, getting cut off at the front

indicators.text: getting cut off at the front
indicators.note: cut off at the front means losing the first letter

parts.note: a fright is a sudden shock

explanation.surface: Merely a jolt, as when someone is decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair or morally correct, a synonym of right.

clue.text: Fruit, a volume taking month to come up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

explanation.surface: A book takes a month to be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns A, V and AUG round to give GUAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A guava is a tropical fruit with pink or white flesh.

clue.text: Less common bird control device getting investment by college

indicators.note: getting investment by means being clothed or enclosed around the college letter

parts.note: a scarer frightens birds away from crops

explanation.surface: A rarer scarecrow gadget gets funding from a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is used in its old sense of clothing or surrounding, not finance.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcer means rarer, existing in smaller numbers.

clue.text: US city, fashionable in days gone by

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An American city that was stylish long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city in Illinois, in the United States.

clue.text: Damages drinks can I dropped

indicators.note: dropped means these letters are taken out of the drinks word

parts.note: martinis are cocktails, drinks
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Things get broken when someone lets the drinks can fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb or 'drinks can' a soft-drink tin; it is TIN, removed with I from MARTINIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or damage, so mars equals damages as a verb.

clue.text: President's baseline involved common people

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of baseline are rearranged

explanation.surface: A president's lowest standard of comparison concerned ordinary folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeians were the ordinary citizens of ancient Rome, hence commoners.
